newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering despite weakness - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering despite weakness - EPA.

text.p: Japan continues a gradual economic recovery despite some weakness, and will maintain easy credit to help the recovery, the government said on Friday.
"No one feels that the economy is rapidly recovering, but nor are there bad or worsening factors to worry about," an Economic Planning Agency (EPA) official told reporters.
In a regular report on the health of the economy, the government's economic policy research unit said Japan's recovery remains gradual, although noting elements of weakness.
The report also reiterated earlier remedies for the economy such as deregulation and expansion of domestic demand while maintaining the current easy credit conditions.

The official singled out household spending as the main factor prompting the EPA to insert a cautionary note in its assessment of the economy. Household spending in July fell 4.4 percent from a year earlier to an average 326,257 yen per household.
But the official was quick to add that temporary elements, such as the food poisoning epidemic that swept Japan this summer, contributed to the slack spending in July.
The official said the report maintains that the basic trend of private consumption continues to be in a gradual recovery phase and that private demand remains steady.
As factors which support a gradual increase in production, the report pointed to bright signs in capital spending and housing starts.
The official cited a rise in department store sales and sales of durable goods, as well as increased personal income, as other positive factors supporting gradual recovery.
The government declared in February that the nation's economy had finally come out of the slump that followed the collapse of the "bubble" economy in the early 1990s.
But the EPA has not been able to take its assessment further than a "gradual recovery" since then.
